record.paper_title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Additional supervision for invariant feature learning
record.original_question: Invariant feature learning methods often need extra supervision beyond labels, such as content-preserving transformations or environment indices. What additional supervision signals, including combinations of augmentations, high-dimensional environment descriptors, and richer object or attribute labels, can be identified and used to separate invariant content from spurious features?

evidence.quote: The previously discussed methods in invariant feature learning (Sec. 3.1) require two distinct forms of extra supervision beyond labels Y : i) content-invariant transformations (Sec. 3.1.1), or ii) environment indices (Sec. 3.1.2).
Identifying and exploiting other forms of labels that inform invariant feature learning is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the supervised learning setting in which one observes data $(X, Y)$ drawn from a collection of distributions $\{P_e\}_{e \in \mathcal{E}}$ indexed by environments $e \in \mathcal{E}$, where $X \in \mathcal{X}$ is a high-dimensional input (e.g., an image) generated from underlying latent factors that can be partitioned into a "content" component $Z_c$ (causally related to the label $Y$ and invariant across environments) and a "style" or "spurious" component $Z_s$ (whose relationship to $Y$ may vary across environments). The goal of invariant feature learning is to learn a representation $\Phi: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ such that $\Phi(X)$ depends only on $Z_c$, so that a predictor $f \circ \Phi$ generalizes to unseen environments.

Existing methods for this task typically require, in addition to the labels $Y$, one of the following two forms of extra supervision:
(i) access to content-preserving transformations $T: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ such that $T(X)$ has the same content $Z_c$ as $X$ but possibly different style $Z_s$; or
(ii) an environment index $E \in \mathcal{E}$ attached to each training example.

The problem is to identify and formalize alternative forms of side information beyond labels — for example, combinations of multiple data augmentations, high-dimensional or continuous environment descriptors, auxiliary object or attribute annotations, or other structured metadata — and to design learning procedures and prove identifiability or generalization guarantees showing that such information suffices to separate the invariant content features from the spurious features. Specifically: characterize classes of additional supervision signals $S$ for which there exist representation learners $\Phi$ provably recovering (up to a suitable equivalence) the content factor $Z_c$ from observations $(X, Y, S)$, and exhibit concrete algorithms achieving this.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open research direction in a survey on causal machine learning. While many specific instances (e.g., augmentation-based contrastive learning, continuous environment indices, attribute-based invariance) have been studied, no general characterization of admissible supervision signals with identifiability guarantees has been established, so the broad problem remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Identifying and exploiting other forms of labels that inform invariant feature learning is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is framed as an open research problem in the surveyed area.
